newsitem.title: UK: Recent wheat rises justified - Merrill Lynch analyst.
newsitem.headline: Recent wheat rises justified - Merrill Lynch analyst.

text.p: The current outlook in the wheat market does make a continued upward price move necessary, but recent rises have been justified, according to Randy Mittelstaedt, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"Given the current assessment of conditions, we feel the recent rally to the $4.30-$4.50 level basis Chicago July is appropriate," Mittelstaedt said in Merrill Lynch's Commodity Market Trends.
"With any additional weather snafus from this point forward leading to additional declines in conditions, we feel new contract highs for new crop are quite likely," Mittelstaedt said.

"However, favourable weather from this point forward, resulting in an improvement in conditions, would likely be reflected in prices dropping from current levels as attention would begin to shift to early prospects for this year's spring crop," he said.

Merrill Lynch's estimate for the total U.S. wheat crop is 2.234 billion bushels, compared with 2.282 billion last year. With 1996-97 ending stocks at 460 million bushels and assuming imports of 70 million bushels, total supplies would be 2.764 billion bushels, compared with 2.748 billion in 1996-97.
Thus, "this year's total supply outlook appears, at this time, to be quite similar to 1996-97."
